Using get_seconds() for timestamps is deprecated since it can lead
to overflows on 32-bit systems. While the interface generally doesn't
overflow until year 2106
column2: the specific implementation of the TCP PAWS

column1: algorithm breaks in 2038 when the intermediate signed 32-bit timestamps
overflow.
A related problem is that the local timestamps in CLOCK_REALTIME form
lead to unexpected behavior when settimeofday is called to set the system
clock backwards or forwards by more than 24 days.
While the first problem could be solved by using an overflow-safe method
of comparing the timestamps
column2: a nicer solution is to use a monotonic

column1: clocksource with ktime_get_seconds() that simply doesn't overflow (at
least not until 136 years after boot) and that doesn't change during
settimeofday().
To make 32-bit and 64-bit architectures behave the same way here
also save a few bytes in the tcp_options_received structure
the type to a 32-bit integer
column2: which is now safe on all architectures.

column1: Finally
column2: the ts_recent_stamp field also (confusingly) gets used to store

column1: a jiffies value in tcp_synq_overflow()/tcp_synq_no_recent_overflow().
This is currently safe
column2: but changing the type to 32-bit requires

column1: some small changes there to keep it working.
